newsitem.title: USA: First Bank to acquire U.S. Bancorp for $9 billion.
newsitem.headline: First Bank to acquire U.S. Bancorp for $9 billion.

text.p: First Bank System Inc. of Minneapolis said Thursday that it signed a definitive agreement to acquire U.S. Bancorp, a regional bank in Oregon, for about $9 billion in stock.
The combination will create the 14th-biggest bank in the country in terms of assets, but it will also result in the loss of about 4,000 jobs, the announcement said.
Under the agreement, U.S. Bancorp shareholders will receive, in a tax-free exchange, 0.755 share of First Bank common stock for each U.S. Bancorp share they own.
Based on First Bank's closing stock price of $78.25 Wednesday, the purchase price equals $59.08 a share for holders of U.S. Bancorp, whose shares closed at $48.25 Wednesday.
First Bank said it would take pre-tax charges of $625 million for costs related to the merger, which was expected to close by the end of June.
It also said the deal was expected to add to its earnings per share starting in the second quarter of next year. By 1999, First Bank sees about an 8 percent addition to earnings per share.
First Bank Chairman John Grundhofer will be president and chief executive of the merged bank, which will be called U.S. Bancorp and be based in Minneapolis.
U.S. Bancorp Chairman Gerry Cameron will serve as chairman of the merged bank until his retirement in 1998.
First Bank said it sees pre-tax cost savings of about $340 million from the merger, with combined operating expenses being reduced by 14 percent.
